questions.q: How did Jehoshaphat ally himself with Ahab?
questions.a: Jehoshaphat allied himself with Ahab by having one of his family marry his daughter.

questions.q: What did Jehoshaphat tell the king of Israel to do to find his answer?
questions.a: Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel, “Please first seek the word of Yahweh for your answer.”

questions.q: Why did the king of Israel hate Micaiah the son of Imlah?
questions.a: The king of Israel hated Micaiah because he never prophesied anything good about the king, but only hardships.

questions.q: Who did the prophets say had given Ramoth Gilead into the hand of the king?
questions.a: They all prophesied saying that Yahweh had given Ramoth Gilead into the hand of the king.

questions.q: What did the messenger tell Micaiah the words of the prophets declared to the king?
questions.a: The messenger told Micaiah that the words of the prophets declared good things to the king with one mouth.

questions.q: To what did Micaiah compare Israel when he saw them scattered on the mountains?
questions.a: Micaiah said that he saw all Israel scattered on the mountains, like sheep who have no shepherd.

questions.q: When Micaiah saw Yahweh on his throne where were the hosts of heaven?
questions.a: Micaiah saw Yahweh sitting on his throne, and all the host of heaven were standing on his right hand and on his left.

questions.q: What was Yahweh asking to happen when Ahab went up to Ramoth Gilead?
questions.a: Yahweh was asking for one to entice Ahab, king of Israel, so that he would go up and fall at Ramoth Gilead.

questions.q: To whom was the spirit going to become a lying spirit?
questions.a: The spirit said that he would go out and become a lying spirit in the mouth of all Ahab’s prophets.

questions.q: What did Micaiah say Yahweh had decreed for the king of Israel?
questions.a: Micaiah said that Yahweh had decreed disaster for him.

questions.q: Where was Micaiah to be until the king of Israel returned safely?
questions.a: The king said to put Micaiah in prison until he returned safely.

questions.q: If the king returned safely, what did that mean about Micaiah’s words?
questions.a: Micaiah said that if the king returned safely, then Yahweh had not spoken by him.

questions.q: Who had the king of Aram told the captains to attack?
questions.a: The king of Aram told the captains of his chariots not to attack the soldiers, but instead, to attack only the king of Israel.

questions.q: What did the commanders do when they realized Jehoshaphat was not the king of Israel?
questions.a: When the commanders saw that he was not the king of Israel, they turned back from pursuing him.

questions.q: What time of day was it when Ahab died?
questions.a: About the time that the sun was going down, Ahab died.

commentary.text: —This history we read in 1Ki 22. Abundant riches and honour give large opportunities of doing good, but they are attended with many snares and temptations. Men do not know much of the artifices of Satan and the deceitfulness of their own hearts, when they covet riches with the idea of being able to do good with them. What can hurt those whom God will protect? What can shelter those whom God will destroy? Jehoshaphat is safe in his robes, Ahab killed in his armour; for the race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong. We should be cautious of entangling ourselves in the worldly undertakings of evil men; and still more we should avoid engaging in their sinful projects. But, when they call upon him, God can and will bring his faithful people out of the difficulties and dangers into which they have sinfully run themselves. He has all hearts in his hand, so that he easily rescues them. Blessed is the man that putteth his trust in the Lord.
